comparisons.peer_summary: The company operates through four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking, and Global Markets, with remaining operations recorded in All Other.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose the composition of their consumer-facing banking segments. GS's Platform Solutions segment generates revenue primarily from credit card lending (net interest income) and corporate deposits via transaction banking. Similarly, BAC's Consumer Banking segment is a key component of its four-segment structure, serving individual consumers with banking services, though BAC groups this under a broader Consumer Banking umbrella rather than isolating a dedicated 'Platform Solutions' line. Both disclosures identify consumer credit and deposits as core revenue drivers within their respective retail/platform structures.

sentences.text: Consumer platforms revenues primarily includes net interest income earned on credit card lending activities.
Transaction banking revenues include net interest income attributed to transaction banking deposits.

Through our various bank and nonbank subsidiaries throughout the U.S. and in international markets, we provide a diversified range of banking and nonbank financial services and products through four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.

comparisons.peer_summary: Non-Markets net interest income is used to assess lending and deposit activities apart from Markets volatility, providing investors with an alternative view of underlying fundamentals and operational performance trends for these specific activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures focus on the revenue sources of consumer and deposit activities, specifically highlighting net interest income from lending and deposits as a primary financial metric. GS describes Platform Solutions revenue as primarily net interest income from credit card lending and transaction banking deposits. Citi similarly defines 'Non-Markets net interest income' as a measure to assess performance of its lending, investing, and deposit-raising activities, isolating these fundamental lending/deposit trends from market volatility. Both identify net interest income from these specific activities as a key component of their financial reporting and management assessment.

sentences.text: Consumer platforms revenues primarily includes net interest income earned on credit card lending activities.
Transaction banking revenues include net interest income attributed to transaction banking deposits.

Management uses non-Markets net interest income to assess the performance of Citi's lending, investing (including asset-liability management) and deposit-raising activities, apart from any volatility associated with Markets activities.

Citi believes the use of this non-GAAP measure provides investors, industry analysts and others with an alternative measure to analyze the net interest income trends of Citi's lending, investing and deposit-raising activities, by providing a meaningful depiction of the underlying fundamentals of period-to-period operating results of those activities; improved visibility into management decisions and their impacts on operational performance; and additional comparability to peer companies.

comparisons.peer_summary: Effective in Q2 2024, JPMorganChase combined its former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking segments to form the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), resulting in three reportable segments: Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), CIB, and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), with remaining activities in Corporate.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose the structure of their business segments to explain revenue generation. GS breaks down Platform Solutions into Consumer platforms (credit cards) and Transaction banking (corporate deposits). JPMorgan reorganized into three reportable segments, including Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), which serves consumers and small businesses, and Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), which serves corporate and institutional clients. While the segment names and scopes differ (GS uses 'Platform Solutions' for both consumer and transaction banking, while JPM splits them into CCB and CIB), both disclosures define these specific segments as the vehicles for delivering banking products to their respective client bases.

sentences.text: We provide transaction banking and other services, such as deposit-taking, payment solutions and other cash management services, for corporate and institutional clients.

Effective in the second quarter of 2024, JPMorganChase reorganized its reportable business segments by combining the former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking business segments to form one reportable segment, the Commercial & Investment Bank.

As a result of the reorganization, the Firm has three reportable business segments - Consumer & Community Banking ("CCB"), Commercial & Investment Bank ("CIB") and Asset & Wealth Management ("AWM") - with the remaining activities in Corporate.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is a global financial services firm with significant market positions in Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, and Investment Management, providing diverse products to corporations, governments, financial institutions, and individuals.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures outline the firm's business segments and client focus. GS's Platform Solutions segment serves both individual consumers (via Apple Card) and corporate/institutional clients (via transaction banking). MS describes its segments as Institutional Securities, Wealth Management, and Investment Management, serving corporations, governments, financial institutions, and individuals. While MS does not explicitly detail a 'consumer credit card' segment like GS's Platform Solutions, both firms identify serving a diversified group of clients including individuals and institutions across their main business lines.
